title: Artifact Restoration Pedestal
description: A damaged sci-fi helmet rests on a luxurious silk pouf pedestal in a museum-like environment. The user must perform a multi-step restoration ritual: adjusting spotlight color and intensity, rotating the helmet to identify damage zones, toggling an X-ray wireframe overlay, tuning environment reflectivity on the pouf, scaling the pedestal, and finally triggering a particle-based repair animation that visually heals the helmet's damage.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads DamagedHelmet.glb and SpecularSilkPouf.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the SpecularSilkPouf centered at the origin as a pedestal, scaled to 2x. Position the DamagedHelmet on top of the pouf, hovering slightly above its surface. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 6) looking at the origin. Add OrbitControls for camera navigation. Create an ambient light (intensity 0.3) and one SpotLight (white, intensity 2) aimed at the helmet from above-right. Add a dark gradient background using scene.background with a Color. Build a dat.gui panel with these controls: (1) a color picker that changes the SpotLight color, (2) a slider (0-5) for SpotLight intensity, (3) a slider (0-360) for helmet Y-axis rotation in degrees, (4) a toggle checkbox that switches the helmet material to wireframe mode (iterate all meshes in the helmet group and toggle material.wireframe), (5) a slider (0-1) for the pouf's material roughness (iterate pouf meshes and set material.roughness), (6) a slider (0.5-3.0) for pouf uniform scale, (7) a 'Restore Helmet' button. When the Restore button is clicked, spawn 200 small sphere particles (radius 0.02, emissive golden material) at random positions within a radius of 2 around the helmet. Animate them over 3 seconds converging toward the helmet center using requestAnimationFrame with lerp, then remove them and briefly flash the helmet emissive to white for 0.5 seconds before fading back. Validate that spotlight intensity stays within 0-5 and pouf scale within 0.5-3.0 by clamping values. Add a subtle continuous idle animation: the helmet bobs up and down 0.1 units using Math.sin on elapsed time. Ensure proper render loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop.
